GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g., semaglutide, tirzepatide) mimic a natural gut hormone that calms hunger and slows stomach emptying. In 68-week clinical trials, adults with obesity lost ≈ 15 % of their starting weight—about 35 lb for someone at 230 lb—when the medication was paired with balanced nutrition and regular activity.

The most common side-effects are nausea, early fullness, and mild GI discomfort; these typically fade after the first few weeks. Eating smaller protein-rich meals, staying well-hydrated, and following a gradual dose-increase schedule can ease the adjustment.

NO… GLP-1 cannot make users drop 2 dress sizes instantly. 

The science behind GLP-1’s ability to mute food noise is real…

But it’s NOT magic.

YES… there will most likely be side effects such as:

📌Cooking becoming unpleasant — smell of food frying/baking becomes tough to bear.

📌Fatigue — energy levels may dip before they stabilize
